name: Acropolis
description: The rock above the city with the ruins of the Parthenon, the Erechtheion and, on the south slope, the Theatre of Dionysus.

name: Syntagma Square
places: Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, Syntagma Square
description: The square in front of the Greek parliament, scene of the city’s big protests. Guards change at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

name: National Archaeological Museum
description: Greece’s largest archaeological museum, with ancient sculpture, bronzes, gold from Mycenae and the Antikythera mechanism.

name: Acropolis Museum
description: A modern glass museum at the foot of the Acropolis, holding the sculptures and finds from the hill.

name: Ancient Agora
description: The ruins of ancient Athens’ marketplace and civic centre, with the Temple of Hephaestus and the rebuilt Stoa of Attalos.

name: Kerameikos
description: The ancient city cemetery just outside the old walls, with grave monuments along the Street of Tombs and a small museum.

name: Pnyx
description: The hill where the citizens’ assembly of ancient Athens met, with a view across to the Acropolis.

name: Omonia Square
description: One of the city’s main squares, a busy traffic hub where several big avenues meet.

name: Exarchia Square
description: The central square of Exarchia, a neighbourhood long known for students, bookshops and left-wing and anarchist politics.

name: Athens Polytechnic
description: The 19th-century university campus where a tank broke through the gate to end the student uprising against the junta in November 1973.
